source:
@@U03119@@
(Sniffing about.)

@@U03120@@
I must say,
as I wander among these modest fires,
I feel quite the foreigner. They're mostly
naked as jaybirds, only here and there
do I see a shift. The 斯芬克斯们 are shameless,
the griffins downright impudent, and all these
winged and curly fleeced things
that display themselves fore and aft!
I have to admit, of course,
that at heart we're as indecent as the next,
but this antique style I find a bit too intense.
It needs mastering, reforming,
in the modern style,
to reflect the new sensibility,
a bit of plaster here and there,
if you know what I mean.
What a repulsive lot!
But I mustn't let it get the better of me.
I'll greet them courteously;
after all, I’m a guest.
Greetings, fair ladies!
And greetings to you, wise old grayfins!

@@U03122@@
(Snarling.)

@@U03123@@
Grayfins!
Not grayfins!
Griffins! Ah!
How dare you call anyone gray!
A word's sound tells you its origin.
Gray, grouchy, grim, gruesome,
grating, grave, groaning.
Etymologically they all agree,
it’s just that we don’t agree with them.
translation:
@@U03119@@
（嗅了嗅。）

@@U03120@@
我必须说，
当我在这些温和的火堆中漫步时，
我感觉自己很像外国人。他们大多是
像松鸦一样赤身露体，只在这里和那里
我看到转变了吗？斯芬克斯人真是无耻，
狮鹫们完全无礼，而所有这些
有翅膀和卷曲的羊毛制品
前后展示自己！
当然，我必须承认，
本质上我们和其他人一样不雅，
但我觉得这种古色古香的风格有点太强烈了。
它需要掌握、改造、
在现代风格中，
来体现新的感性，
到处都是一点石膏，
如果你明白我的意思。
多么令人厌恶的一批啊！
但我不能让它战胜我。
我会礼貌地跟他们打招呼；
毕竟我是客人。
问候，美丽的女士们！
向您致意，聪明的老灰鳍鱼！

@@U03122@@
（咆哮。）

@@U03123@@
灰鳍鱼！
不是灰鳍鱼！
狮鹫！啊!
你怎么敢说别人是灰色的！
一个词的发音告诉你它的起源。
灰色的、脾气暴躁的、冷酷的、可怕的，
刺耳的声音、严肃的声音、呻吟声。
从词源学上来说，他们都同意，
只是我们不同意他们的观点。
